text: Y'all, I ain't gonna hold you.
When Gout Gout ran 1967 back in April, I said it was fake.
And that little comment went everywhere.
Yahoo, Sport Bible, Runner's Tribe, they all quoted me.
And a whole bunch of y'all called me a hater.
So I went back and pulled every race he ran,
every time, every wind reading, every dude in them races.
And by the time I'm done, y'all gonna see exactly
why I said what I said.

Gout Gout was born December 29th, 2007 in Ipswich, Queensland. His momma and daddy came from South Sudan. He was out there playing soccer when his coach, Di Sheppard, seen him. And her story crazy. She ain't have no track background at all. Back in the early 2000s, she was working at a grocery store, and her son was a fast little kid at Ipswich Grammar. They told her only people who work at the school can coach, so she quit the grocery store and took a job hand in hand.

Handing out school uniforms, just so she could coach. Years later, she see this tall, skinny kid running around with his homies, and she said, who dat? I want him. And she been his only coach ever since.
Thanks, guys.
Thank you.
Then in December 2024, at 16, he ran 20.04 in the 200 at the all-schools meet. That broke Peter Norman
record from the 1968 Olympics. 56 years, y'all. And it was faster than Usain Bolt ran at 16.
A couple months before that, Adidas signed him, and folks online started throwing numbers round.
4 million, 6 million. Ain't nobody ever confirmed the number. Not Adidas, not his manager, nobody.
But just like that, everybody started calling him the next Usain Bolt.

But here go the first thing I noticed. Before 2026, every time this dude went under 10 seconds or under 20 seconds, it was wind aided. 1004 with a 3.4 tailwind. 1998 with a 3.4. 999 twice in one day with a 3.5 and a 2.6. 1984 with a 2.2. The legal limit is 2.0. And every last one of them was ran at home.
That's all.
Yeah, in 2025 he went overseas and ran 20.02 in the Czech Republic with zero win. That's the one legal
time everybody gonna throw at me. But put him in a real championship, the world championships in Tokyo,
and he run 20.23 in his heat, 20.36 in the semi, and he ain't even make the final.
Then come 2026, his first race of the year. February 21st in Brisbane, he run 10 flat in the hundred,
win plus 0.9. Legal, but look at the rest of that meet. Six of the win readings that day was over
the limit, and one of the men's hundreds was a plus 2.8. Then the rest of the season,
10-20, 10-19, 10-44, 10-21, he ain't never came close to that 10 flat again.

And the 200 was the same story. At the Queensland Champs, he ran 20.59 and 20.42, and he said he was sick. Then at the Maurie Plant meet in Melbourne, in the rain, Lachlan Kennedy went and beat him, 20.38 to 20.43. So going into Nationals, his best 200 of the year was 20.42.

Now here go the race. April 12th, Sydney, the national championships. In the morning heat, he run 2011. That afternoon in the final, 1967, and the win gauge say plus 1.7. Now listen, the women's 200 final right before them read plus 2.3. Illegal. Same track, same afternoon, minutes apart. And look at the men's final.

Seven of the eight dudes ran a personal best, and every single one of them ran way faster than they did in the heat that morning. Aidan Murphy came in with a 2041 best and ran 1988. Yeah, world athletics ratified it, I know. The gauge said legal. But I'm telling y'all, that race was windy. Ain't no way a whole final PR the same day by accident.

Now let's go down the line. Every dude in that final and what he ran his very next 200. Gout, 1967. His next 200, Oslo, 2060. Almost a full second slower. Aidan Murphy, 1988. Next race, the Oceania champs, 2028 in the heat, 2005 in the final.

Calab Law, 2021. Next race, Tokyo, 2085. Christopher Ius, 2026. Next race, 2102 in the heat, 2068 in the final. Archer McHugh, 2037. He ain't run another 200 the rest of the year. Rory Easton, 2037. Next race, 2142 in the heat, and he ain't even finished the final.

Sebastian Milverton, 2083. Ain't run another 200 all year. And Joseph Ayoade, the only dude who ain't PR in Sydney, he the only one who went faster after. So seven dudes ran a personal best in that final and not one of them, not one ever ran that fast again the rest of the year. Y'all tell me that wasn't the win.
Thanks for watching.
Thanks for watching.

Now here go where it get crazy. Two months later in Oslo, his Diamond League debut, he ran 20-60 and finished 6th. Then he ran 150 in Ostrava and got 3rd. So June 29th, I went on TikTok and I said this.
Then July 4th at the Preclassic in Eugene, Tate Taylor ran 1975 into a minus point nine headwind.
Gout was supposed to be in that race. He pulled out saying tightness. Four days later he tore
his hamstring at practice and he was out of the world under 20s. Now I ain't his doctor,
but I said it on June 29th and everything happened exactly how I said it would.
So here go my verdict. Take away that one day in Sydney and Gout Gout ain't never broke 20 legal.
Not one time. His next best legal time is 2002. All year long in 2026, outside of Sydney,
he was running 20.4, 20.5, 20.6. Meanwhile, Tate Taylor ran 1975 into a headwind. So no,
I don't believe that 1967. That wasn't Australia's fastest man. That was Australia's windiest day.
I said it in April and I'm saying it again. Tell me in the comments if y'all still think I'm a hater.
